title: Multi-omics and in silico evidence reveal perospirone-induced developmental neurotoxicity in zebrafish via AKT/FOXO3a-mediated apoptosis.
authors: Feng, Zhe; Zhu, Lisheng; Li, Wentian; Wang, Fang; Cheng, Qianqian; Yang, Huihui; Huang, Yuqing; Gao, Wenqi; Lu, Hui; Wang, Junbao; Xiao, Han; Gong, Hongjian
one_liner_zh: 该文研究perospirone对斑马鱼的发育神经毒性，涉及AKT/FOXO3a凋亡通路和分子对接，但核心是毒理学而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Perospirone, an atypical antipsychotic increasingly detected in aquatic environments, raises concerns regarding potential developmental hazards in early vertebrates. As an emerging personal care product (PPCP) contaminant, its developmental neurotoxicity remains poorly characterized. To evaluate its biological effects, zebrafish embryos were exposed to perospirone (nominal 0.1, 1, 10 mg/L) from 5 to 120 hpf. At 5 dpf, larvae exposed to 1 mg/L displayed increased locomotion with anxiety-like features, whereas exposure to 10 mg/L was associated with reduced body length and hyperactivity suppression, together with elevated Caspase 9 and Pro- Caspase 3 expression consistent with apoptosis activation. Neurotransmitter profiling revealed an increase in 5-HIAA and decreases in dopamine and glutamine, accompanied by transcriptomic enrichment of pathways related to serotonergic signaling, oxidative stress, and FOXO/AKT regulation. Besides, molecular docking revealed high-affinity perospirone-AKT1 binding (-7.88 kcal/mol). These multi-omics findings establish that perospirone-induced developmental neurotoxicity stems from AKT/FOXO3a-mediated apoptosis, providing critical insights into its neurotoxicological profile and environmental risks as an emerging pharmaceutical contaminant.
abstract_zh: 哌罗匹隆（Perospirone）是一种非典型抗精神病药物，在水生环境中被越来越多地检出，引发了对早期脊椎动物潜在发育危害的担忧。作为一种新兴的个人护理产品（PPCP）污染物，其发育神经毒性仍缺乏充分表征。为评估其生物学效应，斑马鱼胚胎从5至120小时受精后（hpf）暴露于哌罗匹隆（名义浓度0.1、1、10 mg/L）。在5天受精后（dpf），暴露于1 mg/L的幼鱼表现出运动活性增加并伴有焦虑样特征，而暴露于10 mg/L则与体长减少和过度活跃抑制相关，同时Caspase 9和Pro-Caspase 3表达升高，与凋亡激活一致。神经递质谱分析显示5-HIAA增加，多巴胺和谷氨酰胺减少，并伴随与血清素能信号传导、氧化应激及FOXO/AKT调控相关通路的转录组富集。此外，分子对接揭示哌罗匹隆与AKT1具有高亲和力结合（-7.88 kcal/mol）。这些多组学发现确立了哌罗匹隆诱导的发育神经毒性源于AKT/FOXO3a介导的凋亡，为其作为新兴药物污染物的神经毒理学特征和环境风险提供了关键见解。
